key_insight: Adding preferential and differential diffusion to a tabulated-chemistry RANS model substantially improves prediction of lean hydrogen flame structure and heat release.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, cost-effective CFD of hydrogen burners where thermo-diffusive effects can strongly alter stability, flame length, and temperature fields.
method: Extend tabulated chemistry to RANS with transport equations for progress variable and mixture fraction.
Include mixture-averaged diffusion plus Soret effect and couple turbulence–chemistry interaction through a presumed PDF.
Compare against a unity-Lewis-number variant and a table-only thermo-diffusive model, using DNS as reference.
evidence_signal: Against DNS for a lean premixed H2-air slot burner at Re=5500 and 11000, the model reproduces flame length, heat-release distribution, and the equivalence-ratio/super-adiabatic temperature branches.
watch_item: Accuracy still depends on the chosen turbulence closures, especially for turbulent diffusion, scalar dissipation rate, and Reynolds stresses.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
